title: PostgreSQL Fundamentals
outcome: Use relational modeling and SQL deliberately: keys, constraints, joins, transactions, indexes, and query reasoning.
artifact: A TaskFlow relational sketch plus SQL exercises that create, query, join, update, and constrain representative data.
labSteps: Model users, workspaces, membership, boards, lists, and tasks with primary/foreign keys on paper first.
Create a small local schema and insert data that exercises one-to-many and many-to-many relationships.
Write joins by hand and predict row counts before executing them.
Add unique/check/not-null constraints and intentionally violate each to observe database enforcement.
Wrap a multi-step change in a transaction and prove rollback preserves consistency.
Create an index for a real filter/sort pattern and compare EXPLAIN output conceptually.
failureModes: Treating IDs as the only integrity mechanism
Missing composite uniqueness on membership-like tables
N+1 query patterns hidden by application loops
Adding indexes without understanding query patterns
mastery: Can read and write core SQL
Can justify an index from a query
principles: Model data around entities, relationships, constraints, and access patterns before writing application queries.
Use transactions when multiple writes must succeed or fail as one unit.
Add indexes to support real query patterns, not every column indiscriminately.
Let database constraints defend invariants that must remain true regardless of application code.
